project.name: JJ's ERP
project.url: local QA copy (production build) — target https://jjs.ahmad-zaven.io
project.version: fixes on top of commit e4c1e01

summary: All blockers and majors are fixed and re-tested on a fresh server: no double credit or double collection, Syrian-pound debts settle exactly, the live rate is in new pounds, and pounds products and suppliers save. Build, type check, all 9 API suites, the browser tour and the click-through flows pass. Two product questions stay open for the client (orders in fives, sample data).

scope.notes: Tested on a throwaway copy (own data folder, production build) with the sample data and the same env-var logins as the Coolify deploy. Printers, barcode scanner, the real exchange-rate API (no key) and the live VPS were not tested. Some findings were found by reading the code and are marked as such in Cause.

findings.title: Return then cancel gives the client the money and the stock back twice
steps: Make an order of 5 items on credit for a client ($9.50)
Distribution → **Returns**: return all 5 against that invoice, settlement **credit**
findings.expected: The cancel is refused (or only cancels what was not returned). The client ends at $0.
findings.actual: Cancel is accepted. Client balance went 0 → −9.50 → 0 → **+9.50** (free credit). Stock is added back twice. With a **refund** return, the cash box pays out twice.
findings.cause: `server/services/orders.ts:456-470` (`cancelOrder`) does not look at returns already recorded on the order. Reproduced: `qa/flows/money-bugs.mjs` step #1.
findings.fix: Refuse cancel when the order has returns (message: "This invoice has returns — cancel the returns first"), or cancel only the not-returned part.
findings.retest: Re-run in `qa/flows/retest.mjs` on a fresh server: cancel after a return is refused (409 order_has_returns, Arabic + English message); client balance stays 0.

findings.title: A delivery collects money the client already paid at the shop
steps: Make a delivery order on credit ($12.50)
Client pays $12.50 on their account (client page → **Record payment**)
Open **Deliveries**: the order still says $12.50 to collect
findings.expected: The delivery shows nothing left to collect, because the client's debt is already paid.
findings.actual: The driver is told to collect $12.50 again; after collecting, the client is at **+$12.50** credit and the box has the money twice. The daily-close "did not pay" list has the same blind spot.
findings.cause: `orderRemaining` (`server/services/orders.ts:361`) only uses the order's own `paidAmount`; account payments (`server/routes/clients.ts:342`) are never linked to orders. Reproduced: `qa/flows/money-bugs.mjs` step #2.
findings.fix: Cap what is left to collect by the client's real debt (never more than what they owe), or apply account payments to their oldest open invoices.
findings.retest: Re-run in `qa/flows/retest.mjs` on a fresh server: after an account payment the Deliveries screen shows 0 to collect, the driver collects 0, balance stays 0. Same rule in the daily-close unpaid list. Invoice-tied payments now settle their own invoice first (`openClientCharges`, server/services/money.ts).

findings.title: Syrian-pound debt paid in exact pounds still shows a small dollar debt
findings.actual: Order says paid, but the client still owes **$0.80**; it shows in ageing, the money cloud and statements. The same happens for any SYP part payment when the rate moves.
findings.cause: Charge is valued at the order's rate, payment at today's rate (`server/services/orders.ts:348` vs `:413`, `:429`). Reproduced: `qa/flows/money-bugs.mjs` step #3.
findings.fix: When a payment is in the same currency as the invoice, value it at the invoice's own rate (or keep SYP balances in SYP).
findings.retest: Re-run in `qa/flows/retest.mjs` on a fresh server: 1,950 SYP order at 130, rate moved to 140, paid 1,950 SYP → balance exactly 0.

findings.title: Paying a supplier the exact Syrian-pound amount can leave a balance or be refused
findings.expected: The invoice is fully paid, nothing left.
findings.actual: After a rate rise, part of the invoice stays due (536,924 SYP was left in our test across two invoices). After a rate fall the code would refuse it as overpaid.
findings.cause: Same cause as QA-003: `server/services/wholesale.ts:313-333` (`paySupplier`) converts at today's rate while the due amount uses the purchase-day rate. Partly reproduced: `qa/flows/supplier-syp.mjs`.
findings.fix: Same fix as QA-003 (settle same-currency payments in that currency).
findings.retest: Re-run in `qa/flows/retest.mjs` on a fresh server: 10,000 SYP invoice paid with 10,000 SYP after the rate fell (130→120) and rose (140→150): accepted, nothing left due.

findings.title: Closing a past day counts cash from later days as "short"
steps: Go back to yesterday and close it, typing the amount the screen shows
findings.actual: The $100 from today is recorded as a cash difference on yesterday (found in code, not run — needs two calendar days).
findings.cause: `server/routes/days.ts:170` uses the whole box balance as expected; the screen (`days.ts:70-71,100`) uses opening + that day's moves.
findings.fix: Use the same formula on save as on screen (moves up to that date), or only allow closing days in order.
findings.retest: `qa/flows/close-past-day.mjs`: a $100 cash move dated tomorrow, today closed with the screen's amount → recorded difference 0.

findings.title: Returns give back the wrong amount when the invoice had free items
steps: Invoice with 5 free items (loyalty or subscription) + 5 paid items at $3
findings.expected: Nothing is credited for free items; returning the paid ones credits $15.
findings.actual: Free items are credited ($3.75) and paid ones under-credited ($11.25), because every unit gets the same share of the discount (found in code).
findings.cause: `server/services/wholesale.ts:103-105` uses one ratio `1 − discount/subtotal` for every line.
findings.fix: Price each returned line from its own line total and free quantity.
findings.retest: Re-run in `qa/flows/retest.mjs` on a fresh server: 5 free (loyalty) items returned → credit 0; 5 paid items → credit equals what was paid (16.25).

findings.title: Changing or resetting a staff password does not sign that person out
steps: Sign in as member on phone A
Admin resets the member's password on Users
findings.expected: Phone A is signed out (as the client portal already does).
findings.actual: Phone A stays signed in for up to 30 days. A lost phone or a fired employee keeps access until the admin deactivates the user.
findings.cause: `server/routes/users.ts:108` and `server/routes/auth.ts:120` don't delete the user's sessions (portal does: `server/routes/clients.ts:601`).
findings.fix: Delete that user's sessions on admin reset; on self-change keep only the current session.
findings.retest: Re-run in `qa/flows/retest.mjs` on a fresh server: admin reset signs the old phone out (401); changing your own password keeps this device and signs the others out.

findings.title: Cancelling a delivered order after the cash was handed over puts the driver's box negative
steps: Close: hand the driver's cash to the main box
findings.expected: The refund comes out of the box that now holds the money (main box), dated today.
findings.actual: The driver's box goes to −$30 and silently eats their next day's takings (found in code).
findings.cause: `server/services/orders.ts:464` reverses into the original box on the order's date.
findings.fix: Reverse into the main box when the driver's cash was handed over; date it today.
findings.retest: Re-run in `qa/flows/retest.mjs` on a fresh server: delivery cash handed in, then order cancelled → refund taken from the main box, driver box stays 0.

findings.title: Assets page goes blank on refresh or direct link
steps: Press refresh (or reopen the installed app on that page)
findings.cause: The page URL `/assets` is the same as the folder for the app's built files (`server/app.ts:45-47`).
findings.fix: Rename the page route to `/fixed-assets` (and its menu link), keep a redirect from the old link inside the app.
findings.retest: Re-run in `qa/flows/retest.mjs` on a fresh server: page moved to /fixed-assets (200); old /assets links redirect there. UI tour passes.

findings.title: Custom roles can see costs through the day summary and CSV export
steps: Make a custom role with **reports: export** (or dashboard view) but no **see costs**
Export the orders or products CSV
findings.actual: CSV has cost and margin; `/api/reports/five` returns goods cost and profit. Default Manager and Member are NOT affected.
findings.fix: Drop cost columns/kinds without `see_cost`; mask the five-answers costs like `/reports/day`.
findings.retest: Re-run in `qa/flows/retest.mjs` on a fresh server: five-answers needs see-costs (manager → 403); CSV drops cost/margin columns without see-costs; purchases, supplier debts, expenses and withdrawals exports need their own module permission.

findings.title: Server libraries with known security fixes available
findings.actual: 4 high: body-parser, compression, on-headers (fix with `npm audit fix`, no breaking change); drizzle-orm and zod need a major upgrade (low real risk here: no user-built SQL identifiers).
findings.fix: Run `npm audit fix`, rebuild, run `npm test`. Leave drizzle/zod majors for later.
findings.retest: `npm audit fix`: body-parser, compression and on-headers updated (5 → 2 advisories). drizzle-orm and zod need major upgrades: left for later, they don't apply to how the app uses them.

findings.title: Login has no per-IP limit and the server sends no security headers
findings.expected: The attacker is slowed, not the real admin.
findings.actual: The real admin is locked out for 60s, repeatably; one password can be tried against many usernames freely. No nosniff / frame / referrer headers.
findings.cause: `server/lib/auth.ts:110-127` locks per username in memory; `server/app.ts` adds no headers.
findings.fix: Add per-IP rate limit on `/auth/login` and `/portal/login`; add basic security headers (helmet).
findings.retest: Re-run in `qa/flows/retest.mjs` on a fresh server: nosniff / frame / referrer headers present; 20 wrong logins from one address in 10 min block that address for 10 min (per-username 60s lock kept).

findings.title: A product photo can be an SVG file that runs script
steps: Upload an SVG with script as a product photo (needs menu create — admin only)
findings.actual: Any `data:image/...` accepted and served from the app's own address.
findings.retest: Re-run in `qa/flows/retest.mjs` on a fresh server: saving an SVG product photo → 400; photo routes only serve PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF.

findings.title: Sample data cannot be removed once loaded
findings.area: Settings → Network & cloud → Load sample data
steps: Load sample data on the live server to try things
findings.expected: A way to clear sample data before going live.
findings.actual: No clear/reset; sample clients, products and stock stay in reports.
findings.fix: Either hide the button on the online server, or add **Remove sample data** (only before the first real order). Tell the client not to press it on the live server.
findings.retest: Docker image sets JJS_ONLINE=1: the Load sample data card is hidden there and the server refuses it (403). Laptop copies keep it. Not run under Docker here.

findings.title: Orders "in fives" also applies to walk-in, staff and tasting — but not to accepted portal requests
findings.expected: Rule as the client wants it.
findings.actual: Walk-in, staff purchase and tasting must be 5, 10, 15…; a portal request for 7 is accepted as 7.
findings.cause: `shared/orderQty.ts` applied to every staff order; `server/services/portal.ts:75` skips the check.
findings.fix: Ask the client which order types the fives rule is for, then apply it the same everywhere.

findings.title: "1 orders not delivered yet" — plural on the close screen
findings.retest: Close screen uses "1 order" / "2 orders" in English (4 places). Arabic was already right.

findings.title: CSV cells starting with = + - @ are not neutralised
findings.fix: Prefix such cells with an apostrophe.
findings.retest: CSV text cells starting with = + - @ get a leading apostrophe; numbers stay numbers.

findings.title: A supplier or product in Syrian pounds could not be saved
steps: Add a supplier with currency SYP and no opening balance (or a product priced in SYP)
findings.actual: Refused with "Set the USD → SYP exchange rate first" — even when a rate was set. With prices in new pounds the menu could not be built.
findings.cause: `toUsd(0, "SYP", null)` threw: `server/routes/purchasing.ts:33` and `server/routes/menu.ts:197` passed no rate when the amount was 0.
findings.fix: Converting 0 needs no rate (`server/lib/biz.ts`), and the supplier opening balance only asks for a rate when there is one.
findings.retest: Re-run in `qa/flows/retest.mjs` on a fresh server: on a server with no rate at all, a SYP supplier and a SYP product both save (201).

findings.title: The rate API answers in old pounds; prices are in new pounds
findings.actual: The API gives 14,425 (old pounds); every SYP amount would have been 100× too big.
findings.cause: No handling of the 2026 redenomination (100 old = 1 new).
findings.fix: Rates of 1,000 or more from the API are divided by 100 (`server/services/fx.ts`); the manual-rate box refuses old-pound numbers with a clear message.
findings.retest: `qa/flows/fx-live.mjs` against the real API: 1 USD = 144.25 SYP; 5 × $3 salad = 2,165 SYP.

passed: Re-tests of every fixed finding (`qa/flows/retest.mjs`, `close-past-day.mjs`, `fx-live.mjs`) — all pass
Browser tour of every screen (tests/ui-tour.py) and click-through flows (tests/ui-flows.py) after the fixes
Type check, production build and all 9 API suites (smoke, full day, sync, wholesale, portal, day & route, money, manager, member, deliveries)
First start online: admin, manager and member created from env variables; no open setup page
All screens for Admin, Manager, Member and portal client in Arabic and English on desktop and phone — no page errors, no failed requests (except QA-009)
Arabic is right-to-left everywhere with Arabic dates; phone layouts fit 390px with no sideways scrolling
Member blocked from every forbidden page by URL; manager blocked from users, roles, audit, settings, costing, purchasing, people
Portal clients only see their own orders, requests and notifications; portal and staff logins are separate
Discounts: % capped at 100, amount can't push a total below 0, members can't give discounts
Double deliver and double cancel are refused; quantity 0 and negatives refused
Part payment on an invoice puts the rest on the client's account correctly
Order, purchase and return numbers are unique; server runs on Damascus time (Dockerfile TZ)
No secrets in the repo or the web bundle; Supabase and rate-API keys never sent to the browser or audit log
CSV exports open in Excel with Arabic (UTF-8 BOM)
Deep links work after refresh (except /assets); unknown API routes give a clean 404 message
Backups restore only by exact backup name (no path tricks)
